z-m-25-03.title: Seoyun solution multiplying both sides: where did it fail?
z-m-25-03.topic: Fraction inequalities: check solution multiplying by expression with unknown sign
z-m-25-03.goal: Test claim solution is all real numbers except 2, find error line and correct answer.
z-m-25-03.material: Seoyun solve x/(x−2)>1, real x≠2. Work: 1) multiply both sides by x−2: x>x−2. 2) Rearrange 0>−2, always true. 3) All real x except 2 solve. 4) Answer all reals except 2. [2 1 2 1 2 1 2 2 2 0 2 3 2 0 4 2]
z-m-25-03.thinking.2: Correct and solve by separating signs
z-m-25-03.prereq.1: You can solve linear inequalities; multiplying both sides by negative flips inequality.
z-m-25-03.prereq.2: You know denominator zero makes fraction undefined. [0]
z-m-25-03.s.s1.prompt: If Seoyun right, x/(x−2)>1 for every real x except 2. Substitute and choose values failing inequality.
z-m-25-03.s.s1.hint.0: Choose a few x in her answer, calculate fraction and compare to 1.
z-m-25-03.s.s1.hint.1: Test number greater and less than 2; see where issue dey. [2 2]
z-m-25-03.s.s1.r.a: 3/(3−2)=3>1, so holds. To conflict with her answer, need choose value where inequality fails.
z-m-25-03.s.s1.r.b: 0/(0−2)=0, not >1. It is in answer but fail original inequality.
z-m-25-03.s.s1.r.c: 5/(5−2)=5/3>1, so no conflict with her answer.
z-m-25-03.s.s1.r.d: 1/(1−2)=−1, not >1. Included in answer but not solution.
z-m-25-03.s.s1.explain: 0 and 1 in her answer but fail original, so final answer wrong.
z-m-25-03.s.s2.prompt: Choose first Seoyun line with disallowed operation.
z-m-25-03.s.s2.hint.0: Write result separately when x−2 positive and negative.
z-m-25-03.s.s2.hint.1: For each line, identify operation and whether allowed for every x.
z-m-25-03.s.s2.explain: Line 1 multiply by x−2 without knowing sign. If x−2 negative (x<2), inequality flips to x<x−2, false. Line 2 just simplify; 3–4 follow. So non-solutions x<2 look like solutions. [1 2 2 2 2 2 1 3 4 2]
z-m-25-03.s.s3.prompt: Solve correctly with method you choose. Explain method and final solution.
z-m-25-03.s.s3.hint.0: First solve case x−2 positive and write resulting x range.
z-m-25-03.s.s3.hint.1: Solve negative x−2 case similarly and combine.
z-m-25-03.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Did you test one solution and one nonsolution in original inequality?
z-m-25-03.s.s3.selfAssess.1: How my solution handle missing sign cases in Seoyun solution?
z-m-25-03.s.s3.model.0: Only multiply when x−2 positive, inequality keeps direction and x>x−2 true. If negative, flip to x<x−2, false. Thus solution x>2. [2 2 2 2 2]
z-m-25-03.s.s3.model.1: Move 1 left and combine fractions: 2/(x−2)>0. Numerator positive, so denominator positive; x>2. [1 2 2 0 2 2 2]
z-m-25-03.s.s3.modelNote.1: Another method: move terms and combine fractions rather than multiply.
z-m-25-03.s.s3.model.3: If x−2<0, multiplication flips to false x<x−2; if >0, solution x>2.

z-m-25-05.material:
2 students solve equation √(2x+3) = x (the square root of 2x+3 equals x). All numbers na real numbers.
Gaeun: Squaring both sides give x²−2x−3=0, meaning, x=3 or x=−1. Put both values in original equation, only x=3 work (√9=3).
Doyun: Square root value at least 0, so first I write x≥0. Squaring give x=3 or x=−1, among dem, only 3 meet x≥0.
Both answers na x=3.

z-m-25-05.s.s1.r.a: This judgment think fixing the range before solving as deciding the answer in advance. Check which numbers condition remove from the beginning.
z-m-25-05.s.s1.o.b: Only Doyun solution correct. Putting found values in no count as method
z-m-25-05.s.s1.r.b: This judgment no accept substitution checking as method. Use x=−1 direct check whether substitution remove false root.
z-m-25-05.s.s1.o.c: Both solutions wrong. x=−1 also work after squaring, so solutions na 3 and −1
z-m-25-05.s.s1.r.c: This judgment confuse the squared equation with original equation as same. Plug x=−1 into the original equation.
z-m-25-05.s.s1.o.d: Both solutions correct. The only difference na when dem remove false root
z-m-25-05.s.s1.r.d: This judgment see both methods doing same work at different time.
z-m-25-05.s.s1.explain: Substitution check come after solving, setting condition first narrow range before solving. For this equation both give same result. Next test whether both methods always do same work.

z-m-25-05.s.s2.line.2: The inside of √ must be at least 0, so write the condition 3x+1≥0, meaning, x≥−1/3.
z-m-25-05.s.s2.line.3: Both 0 and 5 satisfy x≥−1/3, so solutions na x=0 or x=5.
z-m-25-05.s.s2.explain: Condition for line 3 only say inside √ must be at least 0. For equation, √(3x+1) must equal x−1, so x−1 too must be at least 0. If x=0, √1=1 but x−1=−1, so dem no equal. Therefore x=0 for line 4 no be solution, and only solution na x=5.
z-m-25-05.s.s3.prompt: Choose which method you go use (check values by putting dem into original equation / write condition before square), then explain with one situation where method more convenient or safe.

z-m-25-05.s.s3.hint.1: Think which side go simpler if roots be complicated numbers.

z-m-25-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You check reason by using equation like √(3x+1)=x−1?
z-m-25-05.s.s3.model.0: I find checking by substitution convenient. When the root is a simple number like 3, I can plug it into the original equation and compare dem both sides right away. If the root becomes a complicated irrational number, substitution is troublesome, so filtering by the condition would be better.

(2,5) has the imaginary roots 1±2i, and (1,1) has the imaginary roots (−1±i√3)/2. Conversely, (5,6) has the two roots 2, 3, both positive, so it is not a counterexample.
